notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: In the models of the PRAXIS category the first point of contact for health questions is always a given medical practice, such as the family doctor or a medical centre, which refers the insured person to a specialist where needed.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on insurance models
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: In the TEL_DIG category the first contact happens by telephone or digitally, for example through a telemedicine centre or an app.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on insurance models
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: In the PHARM category the first point of contact for health questions is a partner pharmacy of the insurer.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on insurance models
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: In the FLEX category several first points of contact are available and the insured person can choose freely between them, for example between a medical practice and a telemedicine centre or between a telemedicine centre and a partner pharmacy.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on insurance models
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Insurers offer different models, so before choosing one the insured person should read the insurance conditions and documents carefully and consider whether the model fits their situation.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on insurance models
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Moving from an insurance without a restricted choice of provider into one with a restricted choice is possible at any time.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 100 para. 2. The plain-language portal states the same asymmetry in everyday words, which is what made the coordinating assistant look the article up; this statement rests on the ordinance.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Moving out of a model with a restricted choice of provider to another form of insurance, or to another insurer, is possible only at the end of a calendar year and only keeping the notice periods that the health insurance act sets for the ordinary change of insurer, while a change of insurer during the calendar year on one of the special grounds the act provides stays open.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 100 paras. 3 and 4. Taken together with the fact before it, this is the asymmetry a caller gets wrong - into a cheaper model at any time, out of it only at the turn of the year.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: When an insured person does not pay premiums or cost sharing that are due, the insurer sends a reminder, then a demand for payment, and finally opens debt enforcement proceedings against them.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on unpaid premiums
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The canton takes over 85 per cent of the claims that led to the issue of a certificate of loss or an equivalent legal title.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on unpaid premiums
notes: The page states the 85 per cent without a date; no valid_through is set.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Cantons may put on a list insured persons who do not meet their duty to pay premiums despite debt enforcement, and on the canton's notification the insurers suspend the taking over of the costs of services for those insured persons, emergency treatment excepted.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on unpaid premiums
notes: The exception for emergency treatment belongs to this sentence and is served with it.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: As soon as the insured person settles the outstanding claims, the insurer tells the responsible cantonal authority that the suspension of cover is to end.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on unpaid premiums
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: By way of exception to the ordinary right to change insurer, an insured person in arrears may not change insurer for as long as the outstanding premiums, cost sharing, default interest and debt enforcement costs are not paid in full; children may not change insurer while such arrears exist for them; and an insured person who has arrears only for their children may change insurer all the same.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 64a para. 6. This is the rule that defeats a caller who has found a cheaper insurer and has an unpaid reminder, and nothing in the concept stated it before. The last sentence, that arrears for the children alone do not block the parent's own change, is the part most often got wrong and the reviewer should check it against the German.
The article reserves the changes of insurer that the act allows on a move or a change of job, which this statement does not carry.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Compulsory health insurance grants benefits in case of illness, accident and maternity, among them examinations and treatment by doctors and in hospital, nursing care and certain non-medical services, and in case of accident the health insurer steps in only where the insured person has no other cover.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits and tariffs
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Every insurer that carries out the compulsory health insurance must cover the same scope of benefits laid down by law and must treat insured persons equally, and may not pay further benefits beyond that scope.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits and tariffs
notes: This is the statement that answers whether it is worth comparing insurers on cover; the reviewer should check that the ban on further benefits is stated as the page states it.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: By law the compulsory health insurance covers only benefits that are effective, appropriate and economical, and benefits that may not meet those criteria, new ones as well as existing ones, are examined in the Health Technology Assessment programme.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits and tariffs
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Where a provider carries out services that are not among the obligatory benefits of the compulsory health insurance, the provider must point that out to the patient.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits and tariffs
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Dental treatment is in principle not covered; only dental treatment made necessary by a serious and unavoidable disease of the masticatory system or by a serious general illness or its consequences, or needed to treat such an illness or its consequences, is paid for, and according to settled case law the list of illnesses that require dental treatment at the expense of the compulsory health insurance is exhaustive.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits and tariffs
notes: KLV Art. 17 carries the list of serious diseases of the masticatory system and Art. 18 the list of serious general illnesses; both lead paragraphs state the condition, and the lists themselves run over dozens of blocks that this citation does not carry.
The page names the ordinance articles that carry the list and cites the leading case; the statement keeps the exhaustiveness as the page states it. From the page's FAQ accordion.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A supplementary insurance for the free choice of hospital throughout Switzerland can still be needed, because the insurer and the canton of residence share the reimbursement only up to what the treatment would have cost in a listed hospital of that canton, and a higher tariff at the treating hospital outside the canton is borne by the insured person or their supplementary insurance.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits and tariffs
notes: From the page's FAQ accordion. This is the concept's reason for existing and the reviewer should read it closely against the German.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The compulsory health insurance covers the full cost of hospital treatment outside the canton of residence in every case where that treatment is necessary for medical reasons, that is in an emergency or where no listed hospital of the canton of residence offers the treatment in question.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits and tariffs
notes: From the page's FAQ accordion.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: An insured person may change insurer at the end of a calendar half-year, keeping a notice period of three months.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 7 para. 1. The reviewer should check that "Kalendersemester" is rendered as the end of a calendar half-year and not as the end of a school term.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: When the new premium is notified, the insured person may change insurer with one month's notice to the end of the month preceding the month from which the new premium applies, and the insurer must notify each insured person of the new premiums approved by the Federal Office of Public Health at least two months in advance.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 7 para. 2. This is the right a caller means when they ask about leaving after a premium rise; the act states it as a notice period and not as a fixed calendar date.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Where an insured person has to leave an insurer because they move their place of residence or change job, the insurance relationship ends at the moment of the move or of starting with the new employer.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 7 para. 3.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The insurance relationship with the previous insurer ends only once the new insurer has told it that the person is insured with it without interruption of cover, and a new insurer that fails to give that notice must compensate the insured person for the damage, in particular the difference in premium.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 7 para. 5. This is the statement that answers whether cover can lapse between two insurers.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Where the previous insurer makes the change of insurer impossible, it must compensate the insured person for the damage that results, in particular the difference in premium.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 7 para. 6.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The previous insurer may not force an insured person who changes insurer to cancel the supplementary insurances taken out with it as well.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 7 para. 7.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Under the agreement on the free movement of persons with the EU, the EFTA convention and the new social security agreement with the United Kingdom the duty to insure follows the place-of-work principle, so every person working in Switzerland, and their non-working family members, must in principle take out health insurance in Switzerland.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on cross-border commuters
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Switzerland has made special agreements with the neighbouring states, among them Germany, France, Italy and Austria, under which people with the citizenship of an EU state who live there may insure themselves in their country of residence instead of Switzerland, which is called the right of option.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on cross-border commuters
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person who does not want to be insured in Switzerland must file an application for exemption from the duty to insure with the competent authority of the canton they work in, within three months of the start of the employment relationship.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on cross-border commuters
notes: The three months run from the start of the employment relationship, not from the move.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: According to a Federal Supreme Court judgment of March 2015 a merely tacit exercise of the right of option is not legally valid, so a cross-border commuter who was insured abroad rather than in Switzerland and never filed a formal application for exemption can still insure themselves in Switzerland under the health insurance act, once the competent authority of the canton they work in confirms that the option has not yet been validly exercised; on that confirmation the Swiss insurer takes the person on.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on cross-border commuters
notes: This is the statement that helps a commuter who assumed for years that they had chosen the foreign system. The page says nothing about reversing an option that was validly exercised.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For France the person must, within three months, fill in the form on the choice of the health insurance system and have it stamped by the French health insurance fund, the caisse primaire d'assurance-maladie, before it is returned to the competent authority of the canton they work in.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on cross-border commuters
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For France a person who is insured in Switzerland and keeps working there but moves to France and wants to be insured there must send a copy of the stamped form to their Swiss health insurer at once, so that the Swiss insurance ends.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on cross-border commuters
notes: The page states this only for France, and the subagent did not generalise it to the other neighbouring states.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For Italy the non-working family members of a cross-border commuter living there must, depending on the circumstances, be insured either in Switzerland or in Italy.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on cross-border commuters
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person who is resident in Switzerland and insured there can in certain cases be treated abroad at the expense of the compulsory health insurance.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits abroad
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The conditions under which the costs of treatment abroad are covered differ according to the country in which the treatment is given and according to the kind of treatment.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on benefits abroad
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The compulsory health insurance covers the costs of treatment given abroad in an emergency, and an emergency exists where an insured person needs medical treatment during a temporary stay abroad and a return journey to Switzerland is not reasonable; there is no emergency where the insured person travels abroad for the purpose of that treatment.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 36 para. 2. This is the statement a caller asking about falling ill on holiday needs, and the last sentence is the one that answers medical tourism.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The Federal Department of Home Affairs designates, after hearing the competent commission, the benefits whose costs the compulsory health insurance covers abroad because they cannot be provided in Switzerland.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 36 para. 1.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The compulsory health insurance covers the costs of a birth that took place abroad where only in that way the child could acquire the citizenship of its mother or father, or where the child would be stateless if it were born in Switzerland.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 36 para. 3.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For treatment abroad that cannot be given in Switzerland, for emergencies abroad and for treatment abroad of cross-border commuters, posted employees, people in the public service and their family members, at most twice the amount that would be reimbursed in Switzerland is covered, and for a birth abroad at most the single amount.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 36 para. 4. The ceiling is the answer to what a caller is left to pay after an expensive emergency abroad, and it is not stated on the FOPH page at all.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: People living in an EU or EFTA state or the United Kingdom who are subject to compulsory Swiss health insurance under the agreement on the free movement of persons, the EFTA convention or the new social security agreement with the United Kingdom have to pay the premiums that apply to their state of residence.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on premiums in the EU, EFTA and the United Kingdom
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: About a third of the Swiss health insurers offer insurance to people living in an EU or EFTA state or the United Kingdom, and some of them are active only in individual EU states.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on premiums in the EU, EFTA and the United Kingdom
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The insurer has to calculate its own premium for each state and to take the cost differences between the states into account, so that the premiums cover the costs caused by the insured people living in each of those states.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on premiums in the EU, EFTA and the United Kingdom
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Switzerland grants a premium reduction to people in modest economic circumstances who are insured under the compulsory health insurance and live in the EU, in EFTA or in the United Kingdom.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on premiums in the EU, EFTA and the United Kingdom
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For the premium reduction of pensioners and their family members living in the EU, in EFTA or in the United Kingdom the Confederation is responsible, and it is carried out by the joint institution under the health insurance act.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on premiums in the EU, EFTA and the United Kingdom
notes: The joint institution is the Gemeinsame Einrichtung KVG, which the page names in German.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For the premium reduction of people employed in Switzerland, of cross-border commuters, of people drawing unemployment insurance benefits and of their family members who live in the EU, in EFTA or in the United Kingdom the canton of residence is responsible, and for cross-border commuters the canton they work in.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on premiums in the EU, EFTA and the United Kingdom
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Insured people living abroad have to share the costs of the medical treatment they receive in Switzerland and in some cases of the treatment they receive abroad.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on insured persons living abroad
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: How much an insured person living abroad shares in those costs is regulated differently depending on the country in which that person is insured.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved FOPH page on insured persons living abroad
notes: The page does not name the countries or give the per-country rules, and the concept says so rather than pointing at the ordinary Swiss cost-sharing amounts, which do not apply here unchanged.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Unless the insurer and the provider have agreed otherwise, it is the insured person who owes the provider the payment for the treatment, and the insured person then has a claim for reimbursement against their insurer, which is the system known as tiers garant; that claim may be assigned to the provider.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 42 para. 1. This is the default, which is why a caller receives the bill themselves and is not being mistreated when they do.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The insurer and the provider may agree that the insurer owes the payment, which is the system known as tiers payant, and in the case of inpatient treatment the insurer owes the share of the payment that falls on it.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 42 para. 2.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The provider has to send the debtor a detailed and comprehensible bill and to give them everything they need in order to check how the payment was calculated and whether the treatment was economical; under the tiers payant system the provider must send the insured person a copy of the bill without being asked.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 42 para. 3. The right to a comprehensible bill and to the basis of the calculation is the answer to a caller who cannot make sense of what they were charged.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The provider has to send the bills to the debtor electronically, and at the request of the insured person sends them on paper free of charge.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 42 para. 3ter, first two sentences. The rest of the paragraph concerns the standard the providers and insurers agree on, which this statement does not carry.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The provider is entitled in justified cases, and at the request of the insured person is obliged in every case, to disclose medical information only to the insurer's medical officer.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 42 para. 5. A caller who does not want their diagnosis to reach the insurer's administration can ask for this.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: No form is needed in order to claim benefits from the compulsory health insurance.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 42 para. 6, which departs from the general rule of the social insurance act.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The duty to hold compulsory health insurance is suspended for people who are subject to the Federal Act on Military Insurance for more than 60 consecutive days.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Federal Health Insurance Act as served by Fedlex
notes: KVG Art. 3 para. 4. The threshold of more than 60 consecutive days is what decides the question, and a shorter service does not suspend anything.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The suspension of the duty to insure begins on the day on which the insured person becomes subject to the military insurance.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 10a para. 1.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The insured person is freed from paying premiums from the start of being subject to the military insurance if they tell their insurer at least eight weeks before it begins, and if they miss that period the insurer stops charging a premium from the next date it can manage, at the latest eight weeks after being told.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 10a para. 2. The eight weeks before the service is the step a caller has to take themselves, and missing it costs premiums.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Where premiums are paid in spite of the suspension, the insurer sets them against premiums that fall due later or pays them back.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 10a para. 5.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The insurer has to report to the cantonal authorities responsible for the premium reduction the people whose duty to insure has been suspended, and to tell them how long the suspension actually lasted.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the Ordinance on Health Insurance as served by Fedlex
notes: KVV Art. 10a para. 7. This matters to a caller who receives a premium reduction, because the canton is told.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 46 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person losing their job registers as early as possible with the RAV for public employment placement, in order both to receive support with the job search and to make their claim to unemployment benefit, and should not wait until the last working day to do so.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SECO page on the first steps after notice
notes: Overlaps the already-served rule that registration must happen at the latest on the first day of claimed benefit, but adds two things that rule lacks - that the single registration serves both the placement service and the benefit claim, and the explicit warning not to wait until the last working day.
The reviewer should check that "public employment placement" is an acceptable rendering of "öffentliche Arbeitsvermittlung".
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: In addition to signing on with the RAV, the person registers for Job-Room, the largest job platform in Switzerland, where various eServices and functions are available to them.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SECO page on the first steps after notice
notes: The page states the Job-Room registration as a further step next to the RAV registration; it does not say whether it is legally required.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Early registration with the RAV together with registration for Job-Room brings two advantages - at the first consultation the RAV personal adviser helps build a job-search strategy tailored to the person's situation, and once registered for Job-Room the person gets preferred access, under the job-registration duty, to job advertisements before they are published publicly.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SECO page on the first steps after notice
notes: Mentions the first consultation only as a stated advantage of early registration; the 15-day invitation rule is served by unemployment-benefit and is not repeated here.
The length of that head start is served by job-registration-duty, which carries the five working days from the page that states them.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person facing job loss or threatened notice starts looking for work immediately, because the law requires them to undertake everything that can reasonably be expected of them to avoid unemployment.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SECO page on the first steps after notice
notes: The page gives the article reference to the unemployment insurance act only; the wording of the article itself is not quoted on the page.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: If the job-search efforts made before registering with the regional employment centre are insufficient, the number of daily allowances is reduced, which can mean receiving no compensation for several weeks at the start of unemployment, in some circumstances even for more than a month.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SECO page on the first steps after notice
notes: The block adds that this period can be longer when waiting days come on top; the waiting days themselves are served by unemployment-daily-allowance and are not stated here.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Entitlement to unemployment benefit can also be suspended temporarily if the person resigns without another job in prospect, or is dismissed through their own fault.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SECO page on the first steps after notice
notes: The page states the possibility but gives no length for the suspension.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The job search has to begin before unemployment actually starts, and under an open-ended employment contract it begins as soon as the person knows the contract will end, whether by oral notice, by receipt of the letter of termination or by their own resignation, for at most the last 3 months before the employment relationship ends.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SECO page on the first steps after notice
notes: The reviewer should check that "maximal während der letzten 3 Monate" is correctly read as a cap on the required search period rather than a permission to start later.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Under a fixed-term or temporary employment contract the job search has to run during the last 3 months of the contract, or during the whole contract period if that is shorter than 3 months.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SECO page on the first steps after notice
