notes: The page says only that special provisions apply and does not spell them out, so the statement does not say whether the person is insured. Those provisions are served by ahv-international-coordination.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Students who give up their residence in Switzerland in order to follow a course of education abroad can continue their AHV insurance if they meet certain conditions.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The conditions themselves are not printed on the page. This adds a case the concepts on leaving Switzerland do not carry.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Nationals of Switzerland, of the EU or of EFTA who live abroad outside the EU or EFTA can insure themselves with the AHV voluntarily and can continue their insurance under certain conditions, in order to prevent a later reduction of their pension because of contribution gaps, and the Swiss embassies and consulates give information about it.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: Adds the voluntary insurance and who may join it, which the released concepts on leaving Switzerland do not carry; it is neither a refund rule nor a rule about drawing a pension abroad.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For nationals of the EU or EFTA and of other states with which Switzerland has concluded a social security agreement, special provisions apply in part to AHV insurance.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The subagent flagged this as the fact most at risk of overlapping the released ahv-agreement-states, which says which states have an agreement and what it coordinates. It is kept because it speaks to insurance coverage rather than to coordination; the reviewer may drop it.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: All persons who are insured with the AHV are liable to pay contributions, with the exception of children, who are insured and entitled to benefits such as children's and orphans' pensions without being liable for contributions themselves.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Married persons without earned income are liable to pay AHV contributions, but their contribution counts as paid once their gainfully employed spouse pays at least twice the minimum contribution to the AHV on their own income.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The page prints no franc amount for the minimum contribution, only the rule of twice that contribution. This is the answer to a newcomer told they must pay although they do not work.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The same applies to insured persons who work in the business of their spouse without drawing a cash wage, so their contribution counts as paid through the gainfully employed spouse.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The page's "Das Gleiche gilt" refers back to the rule of twice the minimum contribution in the preceding sentence; the reviewer should check that the statement carries that link.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The contributions of employees are deducted by the employer from every wage payment and transferred to the compensation office together with the employer's own contribution.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The page states that the employer also pays a contribution but prints no rate or split.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Self-employed persons settle their AHV contributions directly with the compensation office, the contributions are based on the income shown in the assessment for direct federal tax, and the compensation office decides whether someone counts as self-employed for the AHV.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: That the office and not the person decides on self-employment is the part a caller planning to go self-employed most needs.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The contributions of non-employed persons are calculated on the basis of their replacement income and their assets, and non-employed and self-employed persons have to register with the compensation office themselves.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The duty to register oneself is the practical step a newcomer needs and nothing else in the release states it.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Gainfully employed persons pay AHV contributions from 1 January after their 17th birthday until they give up gainful employment, while non-employed persons pay from 1 January after their 20th birthday until they reach the reference age.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: Both ages and both starting dates are printed in the cited block. The page adds that special provisions apply at the reference age without stating them.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person counts as self-employed if they are not employed for their activity and bear the economic risk alone.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The page's own short definition; the detailed criteria live in leaflets the release does not carry.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person counts as non-employed for the AHV if they live in Switzerland and have no earned income or only a small one, for example people who retired early, students, world travellers, people whose unemployment benefit entitlement has run out, and people who live mainly on their assets, on pensions or on support payments.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The page's list also names recipients of an invalidity pension; that example is left out because the invalidity insurance is outside this release.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Non-employed persons are in principle obliged to pay contributions, and their contribution duty begins on 1 January after their 20th birthday and lasts until they reach the reference age.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The page says the contributions go to the AHV, the invalidity insurance and the loss-of-earnings scheme; only the AHV is named here because the others are outside this release.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Whether non-employed persons owe contributions and how much depends on their personal situation, in particular on their assets and their pension income, and under certain conditions the contributions can count as paid through their gainfully employed spouse.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person who has already reached the reference age but continues to work must go on paying AHV contributions, although working pensioners have an exempt amount on which no contributions are due.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: The page names no figure for the exempt amount, so none is given.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Since the law on registered partnership came into force on 1 January 2007, a registered partnership is treated like a marriage for AHV contributions and benefits, the judicial dissolution of the partnership is treated like a divorce, and the surviving partner is treated like a widow or widower.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on insurance and contributions
notes: This is what makes the spouse rules above apply to registered partners. Note that ahv-survivors-pensions states the surviving partner is treated like a widower specifically, whose conditions differ from a widow's; the reviewer should check the two together.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Entitlement to an AHV old-age pension arises on reaching the reference age, begins on the first day of the month following the month in which the reference age is reached, and ends only at the end of the month in which the pensioner dies.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: From 1 January 2025 the reference age for men is 65 years, and the previous reference age of 64 years for women rises in steps of three months a year from that figure; the page also still carries a sentence stating the pre-reform ages of 64 for women and 65 for men.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The publisher's page is inconsistent - one block states the pre-reform ages in the present tense next to the block carrying the rule in force since 1 January 2025. The statement leads with the rule in force and reports the stale sentence as what the page still carries, rather than hiding a defect the reviewer should see.
The figure 64 must stay attached as the base the three-month steps rise from, not as a mere historical note. The page prints no birth-year cohorts.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: From 2028 a single reference age of 65 years applies to women and men.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Women and men can draw their whole old-age pension or a share of it from the first day of the month after they complete their 63rd year of age, while women born in the years 1961 to 1969 can still draw their old-age pension at 62 under special transitional rules on which their compensation office advises.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The cohort 1961 to 1969 and the ages 63 and 62 are the figures most likely to be got wrong and should each be checked against the page. The page does not say what the special transitional rules contain.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: During the period of early drawing there is no entitlement to children's pensions, and whoever defers the pension by at least one and at most five years receives an increased pension for the whole duration of the pension drawing.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The loss of the children's pension during early drawing is a cost a caller asking about early retirement rarely expects. No percentage of increase is printed anywhere on the page.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Early drawing and deferral can be combined, so that one part of the old-age pension is drawn early and another part deferred beyond the reference age, and in a married couple one spouse can draw the pension early while the other defers it.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The page names no proportions for the parts.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: How large the reduction for early drawing or the supplement for deferral turns out is calculated according to actuarial principles.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The page prints no reduction or increase rate, so the statement carries none. The familiar rates should not be added from memory at review.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The reform to stabilise the AHV, known as AHV 21, was accepted in the popular vote of 25 September 2022, and until the changes of the reform enter into force the existing law continues to apply.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The reform page carries no ages, cohorts or rates of its own; all the figures of this concept come from the old-age pensions page.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Whoever wants to draw an AHV old-age pension should submit the registration about three to four months before reaching the reference age, because it can take some time until the compensation office has obtained the necessary documents and calculated the amount of the pension.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The page nowhere says in so many words that the pension is not paid automatically, so the statement keeps the page's own framing - a person who wants to draw it submits a registration. A reviewer may want that sharpened from another source, since a caller often assumes it comes by itself.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: If the compensation office's decision on the amount of the pension takes longer than two months after the entitlement begins, the insured person can ask the competent compensation office to make provisional payments.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The two months run from the start of the entitlement and not from the registration.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For an early drawing of the pension the registration must be submitted at the latest on the last day of the month in which the relevant year of age is completed, otherwise the early drawing can only be claimed with effect from the next following birthday, and a retroactive registration is excluded.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: The page names no age here, only the relevant year of age; the statement keeps that wording rather than importing the age 63 from ahv-reference-age. Missing this deadline costs a whole year, which makes it the most consequential sentence of the concept.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A deferral of the pension has to be declared at the latest within one year after reaching the reference age, by means of a deferral declaration on the normal registration form.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the reference age and old-age pensions
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The Swiss electorate decided on 3 March 2024 to introduce a thirteenth old-age pension, so from the year 2026 an additional monthly pension is paid out every year in December, with the first payment made in December 2026.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on the thirteenth old-age pension
notes: The vote date, the starting year and the first payment are all printed.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Everyone entitled to an old-age pension in December automatically also receives the thirteenth old-age pension, no application is required, and it is paid out together with the December pension.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on the thirteenth old-age pension
notes: This is the one benefit in the topic that needs no application, in contrast with the ordinary old-age pension, which must be registered for.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The thirteenth old-age pension corresponds to one twelfth of the old-age pensions paid out in the calendar year concerned.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on the thirteenth old-age pension
notes: One twelfth is a rule and not an amount; the base is the pensions actually paid out in that calendar year, not the December pension.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Whoever did not draw an old-age pension for the whole calendar year, or whose pension changed in the course of the year, receives the thirteenth old-age pension in accordance with the old-age pensions actually paid out.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on the thirteenth old-age pension
notes: The page gives no formula or monthly fraction for the proration and none should be added.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Children's pensions and additional pensions, as well as special supplements such as supplements for women of the AHV 21 transitional generation, are not taken into account in the thirteenth old-age pension.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on the thirteenth old-age pension
notes: The transitional supplement is named only as an example of what is excluded; the release does not otherwise describe it and this statement does not establish it.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The amount is rounded to whole francs, and an exact calculation is only possible in December because the level of the pension can change in the course of the year.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on the thirteenth old-age pension
notes: Rounding is a rule about how the figure is formed, not an amount. This fact is also the ground for declining to compute a thirteenth pension for a caller.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The thirteenth pension applies only to old-age pensions, and survivors' pensions for widows, widowers and orphans as well as invalidity pensions continue to be paid out twelve times a year.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on the thirteenth old-age pension
notes: This is the limit of the rule and must stay with the concept - a widow or an invalidity pensioner reading about a thirteenth pension will otherwise assume it reaches them. Invalidity pensions are named only as not included.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Switzerland organises provision for old age, death and invalidity in a three-pillar system - the first pillar, the state provision, is meant to secure the existence of the old, the survivors and the invalid; the second pillar, the occupational provision, is meant to let people carry on their previous standard of living; and the third pillar, the private provision, is meant to encourage self-provision as an individual supplement.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: The glossary entry is headed Drei-Säulen-System, and the reviewer should keep the printed wording. The glossary names the supplementary benefits as part of the first pillar; they are outside this release and the statement does not name them.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Inside the first pillar the AHV pays old-age and survivors' pensions and helplessness allowances, which make up the largest part of its benefits, and further benefits such as contributions to aids and to non-profit institutions of help in old age.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: Kept at the level of what the first pillar pays; the rules for claiming are carried by ahv-claiming-a-pension and the survivors' pensions by ahv-survivors-pensions.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The occupational pension is the second pillar of Swiss social provision - it is meant to let insured persons carry on their accustomed standard of living in a reasonable way after retirement, together with the first pillar it is meant to reach a pension income of around 60 per cent of the last salary, and besides old age it insures the risks of death and invalidity.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: The figure of around 60 per cent is printed as a goal of the system and not as an entitlement. The subagent flagged it under the no-amounts rule; the coordinating assistant kept it because it is a design goal rather than a sum a person receives, and the reviewer should confirm or strike it.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The second pillar is run through the employer - insured are all employees who are insured with the AHV and earn an annual salary above the entry threshold the page prints, and every employer with staff subject to compulsory insurance must set up a pension institution entered in the register for occupational provision or join one.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: The page prints the entry threshold as an annual salary figure in francs; it is left out under the no-amounts rule, and the reviewer should check the sentence still reads correctly without it.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The first and the second pillar are financed in different ways - the AHV runs on the pay-as-you-go method, where the economically active generation finances the pensioners and the contributions taken in are used immediately for the benefits with no money saved up, while a pension fund runs on the funded method, where each person's contributions are invested on the capital market and paid back at the end of the insurance period.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: Two glossary entries are cited because the contrast between the two financing methods is what a newcomer needs; the reviewer should check neither entry is stretched.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The loss-of-earnings compensation scheme replaces part of the lost earnings of people who do military service or civil protection service, and since 2005 it also covers the loss of salary on maternity and since 2021 the loss of salary during the other parent's leave; the insurance is compulsory and contributions are paid by everyone who also pays AHV contributions, collected together with them.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: No concept in the release covers this branch, so this is the only place a caller learns it exists. It stays at the level of what the branch insures, with no allowances or daily rates.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Unemployment insurance is the branch that gives employees, who are all insured with it, reasonable replacement for lost earnings, and it pays benefits on unemployment, on weather-related loss of work, on short-time work and on the employer's insolvency, and it also pays for reintegration measures.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: One placing sentence only; the detail is carried by the work-unemployment topic. The block also prints the percentage of insured earnings, which is deliberately left out. The page does not assign this branch to a pillar and neither does the statement.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Accident insurance is the branch that compulsorily insures all employees working in Switzerland against accidents and occupational diseases, and it covers the damage that arises when insured persons have an accident or fall ill through their work, with benefits that include medical treatment and financial support.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: One placing sentence only; the detail is carried by accident-insurance. Premiums are left out under the no-amounts rule.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Health insurance is the branch that is compulsory for the whole resident population of Switzerland and gives all insured persons access to basic medical care, making sure of medical treatment in case of illness, maternity or accident where the treatment is not covered by the accident insurance.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on the social insurance system
notes: One placing sentence only; the detail is carried by the health-insurance topic, and no premium figures are given. The page does not assign this branch to a pillar.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The compensation office keeps an individual AHV account for every insured person and enters in it the annual income reported by employers, and for self-employed and non-employed persons the annual income matching the settled contributions once the tax assessment has arrived.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich pages on the AHV account and contributions
notes: Marked federal because the cantonal page describes the duty of compensation offices in general rather than a Zurich speciality.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The AHV account holds the settled employment income and further contributions, these entries determine the amount of the pension, and an account statement uncovers gaps.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich pages on the AHV account and contributions
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 50 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: An extract from the AHV account is free of charge and helps to discover gaps.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich pages on the AHV account and contributions
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The incomes entered in the AHV account statement must match the gross salary shown on the salary certificates, and income from the previous year may under some circumstances appear in the statement only from October.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich pages on the AHV account and contributions
notes: The October rule is what stops a caller reporting a false gap for the most recent year.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Employers report the contributory annual wages of all their employees to the compensation office with the yearly wage declaration, and the office then fixes the definitive contributions, invoices the employer for the whole social insurance contribution and enters the annual wages in the employees' AHV accounts.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich pages on the AHV account and contributions
notes: Kept here because it is the mechanism by which an entry reaches the account, not a statement of who owes contributions.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A full AHV pension is paid only to a person who has paid AHV contributions for 44 years, and every missing contribution year can lead to a reduction of the pension.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on the AHV account
notes: The figure of 44 years is the yardstick for everything else in this concept and should be checked against the page.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: In many cases contribution gaps can still be closed within five years.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on the AHV account
notes: The page says only "in many cases" and names no condition and no procedure, so the statement must not be read as an entitlement.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: SVA Zurich recommends ordering an AHV account statement every 3 to 5 years, rather towards the end of the year, and checking the entries.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on the AHV account
notes: Marked cantonal because the page attributes the rhythm to SVA Zurich by name; it is an office recommendation and not a federal rule.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A contribution gap often comes from a longer stay abroad or from a longer interruption of earned income, because no AHV contributions are deducted from sickness or accident daily allowances or from an invalidity pension, and a gap can also arise on early retirement, divorce, widowhood or when unemployment daily allowances stop.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on the AHV account
notes: The invalidity pension is named only as an income from which no AHV contributions are deducted; no rule of the invalidity insurance is curated.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Anyone in such a situation is safest contacting the compensation office, which then checks whether a registration as a non-employed person is necessary, so that a reduction of the pension because of contribution gaps can be avoided.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on the AHV account
notes: The page names no deadline for this step and no contribution amount for non-employed persons.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: SVA Zurich is the cantonal AHV compensation office listed for the Canton of Zurich in the national directory of cantonal compensation offices.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved directory of cantonal compensation offices and the SVA Zurich pages
notes: The same block carries the office's postal address and the next its telephone number; both are deliberately left out because the pack serves Zurich office contacts in a topic of its own.
The saved page carries an extraction warning, so the entry should be confirmed against the live page at review.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The cantonal compensation offices are the contact point for persons resident in the canton who are affiliated neither to an association compensation office nor to the compensation office of the Confederation.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved directory of cantonal compensation offices and the SVA Zurich pages
notes: Marked federal because the sentence describes all cantonal offices. Together with the fact before it, it is what makes SVA Zurich the office for a Zurich resident, but the page does not spell that combination out and neither does the statement.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: SVA Zurich transfers AHV pensions on the fifth working day of the month.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved directory of cantonal compensation offices and the SVA Zurich pages
notes: The payment day is named on the page as SVA Zurich's own practice, not as a federal rule, which is what makes this fact cantonal. The same block also names benefits outside this release, which the statement leaves out.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The AHV pays survivors' pensions so that the surviving spouse and children do not fall into financial hardship when a spouse or a parent dies, and there are three kinds of them - the widow's pension, the widower's pension and the orphan's pension.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: The page states no franc amount anywhere, so none is carried in this concept.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A married woman whose husband has died is entitled to a widow's pension if at the time of widowhood she has one or more children, or if at the time of widowhood she has completed her 45th year of age and was married for at least five years.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: The two limbs are alternatives and not cumulative conditions; the reviewer should check that the statement keeps them so.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: If a married woman was married more than once, the years of the marriages are added together for the five-year requirement of the widow's pension.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: The adding-together rule belongs to the five-year condition and not to the child condition.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A divorced woman whose former husband has died is entitled to a widow's pension if she has children and the marriage lasted at least ten years, or if she was older than 45 at the divorce and the marriage lasted at least ten years, or if the youngest child turns 18 after the divorced mother has turned 45.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: The divorced-woman rules use ten years where the married-woman rule uses five. The third alternative is easy to misread and should be checked against the page.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A divorced woman who meets none of those conditions is entitled to a widow's pension until the 18th birthday of the youngest child.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: This residual entitlement applies only to divorced women.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A married man whose spouse has died receives a widower's pension if at the time of widowhood he has one or more children of any age, and the page summarises the widower's pension as being paid for as long as the children are minors.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: There is no age 45 and no minimum duration of marriage for a widower, only the existence of children - the conditions differ from a widow's.

The page carries a tension the statement preserves. Its short answer line says the pension runs while the children are minors, while its body grants it where there are children of any age at the widowhood. The reviewer should decide whether both halves stay.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For the widower's pension, children also include children of the deceased spouse who lived in the joint household and are entitled to an orphan's pension through that death, and foster children previously cared for by the spouses if the surviving spouse adopts them after the widowhood.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: The foster-child condition requires adoption after the widowhood.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: If one partner in a registered partnership dies, the surviving partner is treated in the same way as a widower.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: Registered partners are equated with a widower and not with a widow, and the conditions differ, so this matters for a surviving partner without children.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A divorced man whose former wife has died receives a widower's pension for as long as he has children under 18.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: The page states no duration-of-marriage or age condition here, unlike for a divorced woman.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The AHV pays a child an orphan's pension when the mother or the father dies, and when both parents have died there is an entitlement to two orphan's pensions.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The entitlement to an orphan's pension ends on the 18th birthday, or on completion of education, but at the latest on the 25th birthday.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: Both ages should be checked - 18 as the normal end and 25 as the absolute limit while in education.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: As with old-age pensions, the level of a survivors' pension is determined by the contribution period and by the average income, but only the insured income of the deceased person counts, and if that person had not yet completed their 45th year of age at death a career supplement raises their average income.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: This states what determines the pension and names no amount, because the page prints none and gives no percentage for the career supplement. The subagent flagged it in case a rule about determinants is still felt to be too close to the amounts boundary.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: If a person is entitled to an old-age pension and to a survivors' pension at the same time, only the higher of the two is paid, and the comparison is made between the survivors' pension and the old-age pension increased by the widowhood supplement.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service page on survivors' pensions
notes: The comparison is against the old-age pension raised by the widowhood supplement and not against the plain old-age pension.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Since the agreement on the free movement of persons between the European Community and Switzerland entered into force on 1 June 2002, the relevant EU regulations govern the coordination of the social security systems, and the regulations 883/2004 on coordination and 987/2009 on implementation have been in force since 1 April 2012.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: What this adds to the released ahv-agreement-states is the specific instrument for the EU and EFTA relationship and its dates, which that concept does not carry.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The same coordination rules apply between Switzerland and the EU member states and between Switzerland and the EFTA states, the EU regulations have applied between Switzerland and the other EFTA member states Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway since 1 January 2016, and between Switzerland and Croatia since 1 January 2017.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Because there is no umbrella convention, those regulations do not apply to situations that relate to Switzerland, the EU and EFTA at the same time, since the agreement on the free movement of persons and the EFTA Convention are not linked and each applies only to nationals of its own parties, so the free movement agreement does not apply to a Liechtenstein national who lives in Austria and works in Switzerland.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: This is the exception a general answer would miss, and none of the released concepts carries it. The worked example is the page's own. The page does not say what applies instead, and neither does the statement.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person who works permanently outside Switzerland is no longer insured in Switzerland but in the country of employment from the start of that employment, whereas a person working abroad on a fixed-term basis for a Swiss employer remains insured in Switzerland, which is called a posting, provided they are employed by a Swiss employer, the employer continues to pay their wage and withholds social insurance contributions from it, and they hold the nationality of an EU or EFTA member state or of Switzerland and work in an EU or EFTA state.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: The four conditions are cumulative, and the nationality condition decides whether the posting rules are available at all.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A person who carries on a self-employed activity outside Switzerland is no longer insured in the Swiss social insurance but in the country where they work, different rules apply to someone self-employed in several EU or EFTA countries or in Switzerland at the same time, and a fixed-term activity abroad keeps them insured in Switzerland as a posting if they are self-employed in Switzerland, pay the due contributions to the competent compensation office and work in an EU or EFTA member state.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: The conditions for a self-employed posting differ from the employee ones in that no nationality condition is listed. For someone self-employed in several countries the page gives a referral rather than a rule.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: An employee may be posted to an EU state for a continuous period of at most 24 months and to an EFTA state for at most 12 months, and a posting that exceeds those limits from the outset must be notified to the Federal Social Insurance Office, which examines case by case whether an exceptional agreement can be granted with the consent of the foreign social insurance institution.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: The two durations differ between the EU and EFTA, which is the detail most often got wrong.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The A1 form is the certificate of posting used with EU and EFTA states, it is issued by the competent compensation office for cross-border employment or self-employment, it certifies that Swiss law applies in cases of posting and of simultaneous activities in several states, and it serves as proof towards the institutions of the other states so that a client abroad may not withhold social insurance contributions from the fee.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: What this adds to the released ahv-agreement-states, which carries the principle that only one legal system applies, is the document that proves it, who issues it and what it is for.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The application for a certificate of posting and the A1 form should be filed with the competent compensation office in good time before the work abroad begins, and a non-working spouse who accompanies a posted person abroad may join the compulsory AHV by filing a written declaration of accession with the compensation office competent for the posting within six months of the conditions being met.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: This six-month deadline runs from when the conditions are met. The deadline for a non-contracting state, in fact 12, runs from departure abroad instead, and the two should not be conflated.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: An artist or musician resident in Switzerland remains insured in Switzerland during a performance abroad if they work for a Swiss employer who pays the contributions to the competent compensation office, or perform as self-employed and pay the contributions themselves, and hold the citizenship of an EU or EFTA country or of Switzerland; the page directs them to their compensation office for a performance in an EU or EFTA state if they hold none of those citizenships, and for a performance outside the EU and EFTA whatever their nationality.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: The last part is a referral and not an entitlement, and the statement presents it as one.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A Swiss national or a national of an EU or EFTA member state working in a state with no social security agreement can continue the compulsory Swiss insurance if they work for an employer in Switzerland, were insured for five consecutive years immediately before the assignment abroad and have the employer's consent.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: What this adds to the released ahv-agreement-states, which says which states have an agreement, is the continuation route for a state that has none, with its three cumulative conditions.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: That continuation is possible only on written request, which must be filed with the employer's compensation office within six months of the day on which the employee meets the conditions, after which the insurance can no longer be continued, and the compensation office examines the conditions and issues a ruling open to objection.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: The six-month time limit is forfeiting - the page says the insurance can no longer be continued once it has expired.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: A non-working spouse or registered partner living abroad in a state with no social security agreement is not insured unless they declare accession personally, and the accession must be applied for with the compensation office of the working partner at the latest within six months of departure abroad so that the insurance continues without a gap.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved AHV/IV information service pages on international coordination
notes: This six-month deadline runs from departure abroad, unlike the one in fact 8, which runs from when the conditions are met.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: For a person working in more than one state, the compensation office examines in the individual case which state the person is insured in, and the decisive factors are nationality, whether the person is employed or self-employed, the places of work, the place of residence, and whether there is one employer or several.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on contributions in international situations
notes: Names the deciding office for a multi-state worker and the five factors it weighs, which the federal pages leave as a referral.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Special provisions apply to cross-border commuters, and the compensation office gives information on them.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on contributions in international situations
notes: A pointer rather than a rule, and the only mention of cross-border commuters in this concept. The page states no content for those provisions, so the statement claims none.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: Spouses and registered partners who accompany an employed person abroad can join the AHV if they are not gainfully employed, if the employed partner or parent is insured with the AHV on the basis of a posting or of a continuation of the insurance, and if that partner or parent is not a cross-border commuter.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on contributions in international situations
notes: The three conditions, and in particular the exclusion of cross-border commuters, are not carried by the federal facts of this concept.
The page says the person may join the AHV and the invalidity insurance; only the AHV is named because the other is outside this release.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

facts.statement: The application to join is received by the compensation office responsible for the employed spouse or registered partner, the insurance runs on without interruption if the application arrives within six months of departure abroad, and if it arrives later the insurance begins on the first day of the following month.

provenance.author: assistant (Claude) reading the saved SVA Zurich page on contributions in international situations
notes: The consequence of missing the six-month deadline - that cover starts on the first of the following month rather than being lost - is what the federal facts do not carry.
review: confirmed in a bulk review of 40 facts (Alexander Bobrovsky, 2026-09-23)

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt: Anyone who works during his/her stay in Switzerland or who remains in Switzerland for longer than three months requires a permit. Residence permits are issued by the Cantonal Migration Offices. A distinction is made between short-term residence permits (less than 1 year), annual residence permits (limited) and permanent residence permits (unlimited).

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt: Wer während seines Aufenthaltes in der Schweiz arbeitet oder sich länger als drei Monate in der Schweiz aufhält, benötigt eine Bewilligung. Diese wird von den kantonalen Migrationsämtern erteilt. Es wird unterschieden zwischen Kurzaufenthalts- (weniger als 1 Jahr), Aufenthalts- (befristet) und Niederlassungsbewilligung (unbefristet).

evidence.publisher: Fedlex, the Swiss federal law collection (Federal Chancellery)
evidence.original_excerpt:
Art. 10 Bewilligungspflicht bei Aufenthalt ohne Erwerbstätigkeit

1 Ausländerinnen und Ausländer benötigen für einen Aufenthalt ohne Erwerbstätigkeit bis zu drei Monaten keine Bewilligung; enthält das Visum eine kürzere Aufenthaltsdauer, so gilt diese.

2 Wird ein längerer Aufenthalt ohne Erwerbstätigkeit beabsichtigt, so ist dafür eine Bewilligung erforderlich. Diese ist vor der Einreise in die Schweiz bei der am vorgesehenen Wohnort zuständigen Behörde zu beantragen. Artikel 17 Absatz 2 bleibt vorbehalten.

1 Ausländerinnen und Ausländer, die in der Schweiz eine Erwerbstätigkeit ausüben wollen, benötigen unabhängig von der Aufenthaltsdauer eine Bewilligung. Diese ist bei der am vorgesehenen Arbeitsort zuständigen Behörde zu beantragen.

2 Als Erwerbstätigkeit gilt jede üblicherweise gegen Entgelt ausgeübte unselbständige oder selbständige Tätigkeit, selbst wenn sie unentgeltlich erfolgt.

1 Die Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligung wird für befristete Aufenthalte bis zu einem Jahr erteilt.

evidence.original_excerpt:
Ausweis B EU/EFTA (Aufenthaltsbewilligung)

Schliessen

Ausweis B EU/EFTA (Aufenthaltsbewilligung)

Aufenthalter und Aufenthalterinnen sind ausländische Personen, die sich für einen bestimmten Zweck längerfristig mit oder ohne Erwerbstätigkeit in der Schweiz aufhalten.

Die Aufenthaltsbewilligung der Angehörigen von EU/EFTA-Mitgliedstaaten hat eine Gültigkeitsdauer von fünf Jahren; sie wird erteilt, wenn EU/EFTA-Bürgerinnen und -Bürger den Nachweis einer unbefristeten oder auf mindestens 365 Tage befristeten Anstellung erbringen.

Die Aufenthaltsbewilligung wird um fünf Jahre verlängert, wenn die ausländische Person die Voraussetzungen dafür erfüllt. Bei der ersten Verlängerung kann sie aber auf ein Jahr beschränkt werden, wenn die betreffende Person seit über zwölf aufeinanderfolgenden Monaten unfreiwillig arbeitslos ist. Personen ohne Erwerbstätigkeit aus allen EU/EFTA-Staaten haben Anspruch auf die Bewilligung B EU/EFTA ohne Erwerbstätigkeit, wenn sie genügende finanzielle Mittel sowie eine ausreichende Kranken- und Unfallversicherung nachweisen können.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Ausweis L EU/EFTA (Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligung)

Schliessen

Ausweis L EU/EFTA (Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligung)

Kurzaufenthalter sind Ausländerinnen und Ausländer, die sich befristet, in der Regel für weniger als ein Jahr, für einen bestimmten Aufenthaltszweck mit oder ohne Erwerbstätigkeit in der Schweiz aufhalten.

EU/EFTA-Angehörige haben einen Anspruch auf Erteilung dieser Bewilligung, sofern sie in der Schweiz ein Arbeitsverhältnis zwischen drei Monaten und einem Jahr nachweisen können. Arbeitsverhältnisse unter drei Monaten im Kalenderjahr bedürfen für EU/EFTA-Angehörige keiner Bewilligung, diese sind über das sogenannte Online-Meldeverfahren zu regeln. Die Gültigkeitsdauer der Bewilligung entspricht derjenigen des Arbeitsvertrags. Sie kann bis zu einer Gesamtdauer von weniger als 12 Monaten verlängert werden. Bewilligungen L EU/EFTA ohne Erwerbstätigkeit werden an Stellensuchende aus allen EU/EFTA-Staaten erteilt, dies schafft aber keine Ansprüche aus der Sozialhilfe.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Ausweis Ci EU/EFTA (Aufenthaltsbewilligung mit Erwerbstätigkeit)

Schliessen

Ausweis Ci EU/EFTA (Aufenthaltsbewilligung mit Erwerbstätigkeit)

Die Aufenthaltsbewilligung Ci mit Erwerbstätigkeit ist für Familienangehörige von Beamtinnen und Beamten intergouvernementaler Organisationen und für Mitarbeitende von ausländischen Vertretungen bestimmt. Es handelt sich dabei um die Ehegatten und die Kinder bis zum 25. Altersjahr. Die Gültigkeit ist auf die Dauer der Funktion des Hauptinhabers oder der Hauptinhaberin beschränkt.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Ausweis G EU/EFTA (Grenzgängerbewilligung)

Schliessen

Ausweis G EU/EFTA (Grenzgängerbewilligung)

Als Grenzgängerin und Grenzgänger werden Staatsangehörige der EU/EFTA bezeichnet, die sich in einem EU/EFTA-Staat aufhalten und in der Schweiz arbeiten (Stellenantritt oder Aufnahme einer selbstständigen Erwerbstätigkeit). Grenzgängerinnen und Grenzgänger kehren in der Regel täglich oder mindestens einmal wöchentlich an ihren ausländischen Hauptwohnsitz zurück.

Grenzgängerinnen und Grenzgänger aus den EU/EFTA-Mitgliedstaaten geniessen berufliche und geographische Mobilität. Für sie gelten keine Grenzzonen mehr. Sie können somit überall in der EU/EFTA wohnen und überall in der Schweiz arbeiten, Bedingung ist lediglich die wöchentliche Rückkehr an den ausländischen Wohnort. Die Bewilligung für Grenzgängerinnen und Grenzgänger aus der EU/EFTA ist fünf Jahre gültig, sofern ein Arbeitsvertrag vorliegt, der unbeschränkt oder länger als ein Jahr gültig ist. Wurde der Arbeitsvertrag für eine Gültigkeitsdauer von weniger als einem Jahr, aber länger als drei Monaten abgeschlossen, richtet sich die Gültigkeitsdauer dieser Bewilligung nach der Gültigkeitsdauer des Arbeitsvertrags. Für eine Anstellungsdauer von weniger als drei Monaten gilt das Online-Meldeverfahren.

evidence.original_excerpt:
Navigation

Ausweis Ci (Aufenthaltsbewilligung mit Erwerbstätigkeit)

Die Aufenthaltsbewilligung mit Erwerbstätigkeit ist für Familienangehörige von Beamten intergouvernementaler Organisationen und für Mitglieder ausländischer Vertretungen bestimmt. Es handelt sich dabei um die Ehegatten und die Kinder bis zum 25. Altersjahr. Die Gültigkeit ist auf die Dauer der Funktion des Hauptinhabers beschränkt.

Dieser Ausweis ist kein Nachweis für die Identität des Inhabers/der Inhaberin.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Ausweis G (Grenzgängerbewilligung)

Grenzgänger sind Ausländerinnen oder Ausländer, die ihren Wohnsitz in der ausländischen Grenzzone haben und innerhalb der benachbarten Grenzzone der Schweiz erwerbstätig sind. Als Grenzzonen gelten die Regionen, die in den zwischen der Schweiz und ihren Nachbarstaaten abgeschlossenen Grenzgängerabkommen festgelegt sind. Die Grenzgänger müssen wöchentlich mindestens ein Mal an ihren ausländischen Hauptwohnsitz zurückkehren.

Grenzgängern aus Drittstaaten kann eine Grenzgängerbewilligung nur erteilt werden, wenn sie ein dauerhaftes Anwesenheitsrecht in einem Nachbarstaat der Schweiz besitzen und seit mindestens sechs Monaten in der Grenzzone wohnhaft sind. Außerdem sind die arbeitsmarktlichen Vorschriften zu beachten. In der Regel wird die erstmalige Grenzgängerbewilligung mit einer Gültigkeitsdauer von einem Jahr ausgestellt und ist nur für die Grenzzone des Kantons, welcher die Bewilligung erteilt hat, gültig. Sowohl der Stellenwechsel, wie auch die Aufnahme einer selbständigen Erwerbstätigkeit sind bewilligungspflichtig.

Dieser Ausweis ist kein Nachweis für die Identität des Inhabers/der Inhaberin.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt: Bei den vom SEM ausgestellten Reisedokumenten handelt es sich um fremdenpolizeiliche Ausweise. Mit ihnen kann weder die Identität noch die Staatsangehörigkeit der ausländischen Person nachgewiesen werden.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Wer ein Reisedokument beantragen will, muss bei der zuständigen kantonalen Migrationsbehörde persönlich vorsprechen.

Wird der Ersatz für ein abgelaufenes Reisedokument beantragt, so muss die antragstellende Person dieses der kantonalen Migrationsbehörde zu Handen des SEM abgeben. Das Gesuch ist bei der kantonalen Migrationsbehörde wenn möglich sechs Wochen vor Ablauf der Gültigkeitsdauer des alten Dokuments beziehungsweise vor Antritt der beabsichtigten Reise einzureichen.

Verlust

Als Verlust gilt jegliches Abhandenkommen eines Reisedokuments, auch jenes durch Diebstahl oder vollständige Zerstörung. Die Inhaberin oder der Inhaber des Reisedokuments hat dessen Verlust sofort nach Feststellung der örtlichen Polizeistelle anzuzeigen. Ist der Verlust im Ausland erfolgt, so ist er zusätzlich noch der zuständigen schweizerischen diplomatischen oder konsularischen Vertretung zu melden. Diese leitet die Verlustmeldung an das SEM weiter. Die ausländische Person hat das Reisedokument, dessen Verlust sie gemeldet hat, unaufgefordert zurückzugeben, sobald sie wieder in dessen Besitz gelangt ist.

If you are planning to stay in Switzerland for several years, you will also have to fulfil certain other criteria that will facilitate your long-term professional and social integration. The key factors are your professional and social adaptability, language skills and age.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Die Schweiz kennt bei der Zulassung ausländischer Arbeitskräfte ein duales System. Erwerbstätige aller Qualifikationsstufen aus den EU/EFTA-Staaten erhalten durch das Personenfreizügigkeitsabkommen einfachen Zugang zum Schweizer Arbeitsmarkt. Aus allen anderen Staaten – sogenannte Drittstaaten – erfolgt die Zulassung komplementär zum Freizügigkeitsabkommen. Gemäss Auftrag des Bundesrates können dabei lediglich gut qualifizierte Arbeitskräfte in beschränktem Ausmass zugelassen werden, da diese erfahrungsgemäss bessere langfristige berufliche und soziale Integrationschancen haben als Personen mit tieferen Qualifikationen.

Die Zulassungskriterien sind im Bundesgesetz über die Ausländerinnen und Ausländer und über die Integration AIG und der Verordnung über Zulassung, Aufenthalt und Erwerbstätigkeit aufgeführt. Sie werden in den AIG-Weisungen näher erläutert.

Wir erklären Ihnen zusammenfassend die wichtigsten Zulassungskriterien, damit Sie einerseits verstehen, unter welchen Voraussetzungen die Behörden eine Bewilligung erteilen können und andererseits in der Lage sind, Ihr Gesuch vollständig und gut dokumentiert einzureichen.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Eine Zulassung von Drittstaatsangehörigen zum Schweizer Arbeitsmarkt kann nur erfolgen, wenn diese dem gesamtschweizerischen und gesamtwirtschaftlichen Interesse der Schweiz entspricht. Dabei werden insbesondere die jeweilige Arbeitsmarktsituation, die nachhaltige Wirtschaftsentwicklung und die Integrationsfähigkeit der Ausländerinnen und Ausländer berücksichtigt.

Das gesamtwirtschaftliche Interesse ist vom Gesuchsteller entsprechend zu begründen und zu belegen.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Die Zulassung von Drittstaatsangehörigen ist erst möglich, wenn auf dem inländischen Arbeitsmarkt und auf den Arbeitsmärkten der EU/EFTA-Länder keine Personen mit Vorrang zur Verfügung stehen. Vorrang geniessen Schweizerinnen und Schweizer, Ausländerinnen und Ausländer mit Niederlassungsbewilligung (Ausweis C), Ausländerinnen und Ausländer mit Aufenthaltsbewilligung (Ausweis B, inkl. anerkannte Flüchtlinge), die zu einer Erwerbstätigkeit berechtigt sind, Ausländerinnen und Ausländer mit einer vorläufigen Aufnahme (Ausweis F), Personen, denen vorübergehender Schutz gewährt wurde und die eine Bewilligung zur Aufnahme einer Erwerbstätigkeit besitzen (Ausweis S) sowie alle Personen aus Staaten, mit denen ein Freizügigkeitsabkommen geschlossen wurde (Ausweis L und B). Die Arbeitgeber haben den Nachweis zu erbringen, dass trotz umfassender Suchbemühungen keine geeigneten Arbeitskräfte mit Vorrang rekrutiert werden konnten.

Der Arbeitgeber hat dabei Suchbemühungen glaubhaft zu machen, die in zeitlicher Folge, geografischer Breite und inhaltlich zweckmässiger Art ein echtes Bemühen aufzeigen, die fragliche Stelle mit inländischen Bewerbenden bzw. solchen aus EU/EFTA-Staaten zu besetzen. Eine Kontaktnahme mit Drittstaatsangehörigen sollte erst erfolgen, nachdem solche Suchbemühungen tatsächlich erfolglos geblieben sind.

Die Stellen sind grundsätzlich den Regionalen Arbeitsvermittlungszentren (RAV) zu melden. Eine Ausschreibung im European Employment System (EURES) ist ebenfalls notwendig. Darüber hinaus ist den Behörden darzulegen, dass die Suche über die in der Branche fachspezifischen Rekrutierungskanäle wie Fachzeitschriften, Stellenbörsen, Onlineportalen sowie Social Media, private Vermittlung etc. erfolglos blieb. Geeignete Nachweise sind hier entweder Zeitungsinserate, Bestätigungen der Personalvermittler oder sonstige Dokumente. Oftmals ist eine kurze Übersicht über alle Stellenbewerber mit kurzen Angaben, welche Qualifikationen für eine Anstellung fehlten, hilfreich. In besonderen Fällen können auch besondere Rekrutierungsbemühungen eingefordert werden.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Für Drittstaatsangehörige stellt die Stellenmeldepflicht neben insbesondere dem Vorrang der inländischen Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer oder der Angehörigen von Staaten, mit denen ein Freizügigkeitsabkommen abgeschlossen wurde, eine weitere Zulassungsvoraussetzung dar.

Die Stellenmeldepflicht gilt für diejenigen Berufsgruppen, Tätigkeitsbereiche oder Wirtschaftsregionen, in denen die gesamtschweizerische Arbeitslosenquote 5 Prozent erreicht oder überschreitet. Eine Liste mit den der Meldepflicht unterliegenden Berufsarten wird vom Staatssekretariat für Wirtschaft (SECO) jährlich neu festgelegt:

Liste mit den der Meldepflicht unterliegenden Berufsarten

Mit Drittstaatsangehörigen zu besetzende Stellen in Berufsarten mit einer über dem Schwellenwert liegenden Arbeitslosigkeit unterliegen der Stellenmeldepflicht, sofern nicht die Ausnahmeregelung zur Anwendung gelangt (z. B. Anstellung von bei der öffentlichen Arbeitsvermittlung registrierten Stellensuchenden ungeachtet ihrer Nationalität, betrieblicher Transfer in internationalen Unternehmen von Personen, deren Anstellung mindestens sechs Monate beim gleichen Unternehmen gedauert hat, obligatorische Praktika während der Ausbildung).

Die Stellenmeldepflicht ist durch die zuständige kantonale Behörde zu prüfen. Die Arbeitgeber haben somit den Gesuchen um Erteilung einer Arbeitsbewilligung in Berufsarten mit einer über dem Durchschnitt liegenden Arbeitslosigkeit einen Nachweis über die erfolgte Stellenmeldung beizulegen.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Der Lohn, die Sozialversicherungsbeiträge und die Arbeitsbedingungen für die ausländische Arbeitskraft müssen den orts-, berufs- und branchenüblichen Verhältnissen entsprechen. Einige Branchen legen diese Bedingungen in Gesamtarbeitsverträgen fest, welche national oder zumindest kantonal verbindlich sind. Die Behörden stellen mit der vorgängigen Kontrolle der Lohn- und Arbeitsbedingungen auch sicher, dass die ausländischen Mitarbeitenden nicht missbräuchlichen Arbeitsbedingungen ausgesetzt sind und die inländischen Arbeitskräfte vor Lohndumping geschützt werden.

Der Arbeitgeber fügt dem Gesuch einen schriftlichen Arbeitsvertrag hinzu, der von ihm und dem Arbeitnehmer unterzeichnet ist und mit dem Vermerk versehen wird: «Vertrag gilt nur, wenn die Behörden eine Bewilligung zur Erwerbstätigkeit erteilen». Dies dient der Rechtssicherheit für beide Vertragspartner. Die Verwendung von branchenüblichen Vertragsformularen ist hilfreich für die Behörden.

Arbeitgeber müssen alle Angestellten bei den verschiedenen Sozialversicherungsinstitutionen anmelden. Gute und übersichtliche Informationen dazu bietet der Ratgeber Sozialversicherung, der vom Bundesamt für Sozialversicherungen (BSV) in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Staatssekretariat für Wirtschaft (SECO) erarbeitet wurde.

Ausländische Arbeitskräfte ohne Niederlassungsbewilligung unterliegen zudem der Quellenbesteuerung. Die Arbeitnehmenden sind deshalb bei den Steuerbehörden anzumelden. Anschliessend ist der Arbeitgeber dafür verantwortlich, die Steuer jeweils monatlich vom Lohn abzuziehen und den Steuerbehörden zu überweisen. Weitere Informationen dazu erteilen die kantonalen Steuerbehörden oder die Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung.

Das neue Bundesgesetz über die Schwarzarbeit sieht zum einen Erleichterungen bei der Abrechnung von Sozialversicherungsprämien für kleinere, unselbständige Tätigkeiten vor. Zum anderen wird durch neue Massnahmen und höhere Strafen die Bekämpfung der Schwarzarbeit verbessert. Nicht geändert hat sich der Grundsatz für Arbeitgeber und Ausländerinnen und Ausländer, dass für jede Erwerbstätigkeit – ob bezahlt oder unbezahlt – eine Bewilligung erforderlich ist. Verstösse gegen orts-, berufs- und branchenübliche Lohn- und Arbeitsbedingungen sowie Schwarzarbeitsfälle werden in erster Linie von den kantonalen Behörden oder den in einigen Branchen speziell dafür eingerichteten Fachstellen untersucht und sind strafbar.

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
Zugelassen werden können Führungskräfte, Spezialistinnen und Spezialisten sowie andere qualifizierte Arbeitskräfte. Als qualifizierte Arbeitskräfte gelten in erster Linie Personen mit Hochschul- oder Fachhochschulabschluss sowie mehrjähriger Berufserfahrung. Je nach Beruf oder Spezialisierung können auch Personen mit besonderer fachlicher Ausbildung und mehrjähriger Berufserfahrung zugelassen werden.

Für die Erteilung von Aufenthaltsbewilligungen sind neben den beruflichen Qualifikationen auch Integrationskriterien zu berücksichtigen: berufliche und soziale Anpassungsfähigkeit, die Sprachkenntnisse und das Alter müssen eine nachhaltige Integration in den schweizerischen Arbeitsmarkt und das gesellschaftliche Umfeld erwarten lassen.

Die Qualifikationen werden anhand des Lebenslaufes, der Diplome und Arbeitszeugnisse der ausländischen Arbeitskraft geprüft. Die Behörden benötigen Kopien der Dokumente in Originalsprache sowie übersetzt in einer der Schweizer Amtssprachen oder in Englisch.

Stammen die ausländischen Personen aus Ländern, welche ein wesentlich anderes Schul- und Berufsbildungssystem kennen als die Schweiz, ist es für die Behörden hilfreich, wenn Dokumente vorgelegt werden, die zusätzliche Angaben über die Ausbildungsinstitution sowie die Dauer und den Inhalt der Ausbildung enthalten (bspw. Studienplan, Ausbildungszeugnisse über abgelegte Prüfungsfächer und erzielte Resultate, etc.).

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM
evidence.original_excerpt:
In gewissen Fällen sind bestimmte, gesetzlich geregelte Abweichungen von den Zulassungsvoraussetzungen möglich. Die folgende Übersicht ist nicht abschliessend, stellt aber die häufigsten Fälle dar:

Kader- oder Spezialistentransfer in internationalen Unternehmen Beim betrieblichen Transfer von höherem Kader und unentbehrlichen Spezialisten in internationalen Unternehmen gelangt der Vorrang nicht zur Anwendung.

Praktikum, Aus- und Weiterbildung - in global tätigen Unternehmen (Knowhowtransfer) - Pflichtpraktika während dem Studium

Doktoranden / Postdoktoranden Personen, welche über die universitäre Grundausbildung hinaus ihre Studien oder Forschungsarbeiten an einer anerkannten oder zugelassenen Schweizer Hochschule im Hinblick auf eine Spezialisierung fortführen und damit die optimale Entwicklung von Wissenschaft und Technologie in der Schweiz sicherstellen. Anerkannte oder akkreditierte Schweizer Hochschulen

Familienangehörige Für die Ausübung einer selbstständigen oder unselbständigen Erwerbstätigkeit ist für Familienangehörige von Schweizerinnen und Schweizern, Niedergelassenen sowie Aufenthalterinnen und Aufenthaltern ohne Bewilligung kein zusätzliches Bewilligungsverfahren notwendig. Familienangehörige von Kurzaufenthalterinnen und Kurzaufenthaltern hingegen benötigen eine Bewilligung. Dabei sind die orts- und berufsüblichen Lohn- und Arbeitsbedingungen einzuhalten und die persönlichen Voraussetzungen sind nachzuweisen.

Au-Pair-Angestellte Die Au-pair-Beschäftigung besteht in der zeitlich begrenzten Aufnahme junger Ausländerinnen und Ausländer, die in der Schweiz einreisen, um ihre Sprachkenntnisse zu vervollkommnen und ihre Allgemeinbildung durch eine bessere Kenntnis des Gastlands zu erweitern, durch Familien im Austausch für bestimmte Leistungen (leichte Hausarbeiten und Kinderbetreuung). Au-pair-Angestellte aus Drittstaaten können im Alter zwischen 18 und 25 für einen Aufenthalt von max. 12 Monate zugelassen werden. Sie unterstehen den Erfordernissen des Vorrangs nicht. Weil damit jedoch der Schutzbedarf steigt (Menschenhandel, Ausbeutung), ist die zwingende Vermittlung durch eine in der Schweiz anerkannte Organisation vorgesehen.

Erwerbstätigkeit nach einem Studium in der Schweiz Ausländerinnen und Ausländer können zur Ausübung einer Erwerbstätigkeit ohne Nachweis des Vorrangs zugelassen werden, wenn ihre Erwerbstätigkeit von hohem wissenschaftlichem oder wirtschaftlichem Interesse ist. Diese Regelung gilt nur für Abschlüsse von anerkannten Schweizer Hochschulen (Universitäre Hochschulen und Fachhochschulen). Anerkannte oder akkreditierte Schweizer Hochschulen

evidence.publisher: State Secretariat for Migration SEM

evidence.original_excerpt:
Das elektronische Meldeverfahren kommt ebenfalls für Stellenantritte von bis zu drei Monaten bei einem Unternehmen in der Schweiz zur Anwendung. Es besteht lediglich eine Meldepflicht. Im Falle eines Stellenantritts in der Schweiz, der länger als 3 Monate dauert, muss eine Aufenthaltsbewilligung respektive wenn die Voraussetzungen erfüllt sind, eine Grenzgängerbewilligung eingeholt werden.

Bei einem Stellenantritt bei einem Unternehmen in der Schweiz (Dauer des Arbeitsvertrags bis zu drei Monaten), hat die Meldung spätestens am Tag vor der Arbeitsaufnahme zu erfolgen.

The online notification procedure also applies to companies based in Switzerland that would like to employ foreign workers for periods of up to three months. All that is required is submission of a notification form. If the intention is to employ a worker for longer than three months, then this person must request a Swiss residence permit or must satisfy the requirements for issuance of a cross-border commuter permit.

Companies or self-employed service providers must first create a user profile in the system. Each assignment carried out in Switzerland must be entered into the system at least eight days prior to commencement of work. For foreign workers taking up short-term employment with a company based in Switzerland (work contracts of up to three months in duration), the notification form must be submitted no later than one day prior to the first day of work.

The competent cantonal authorities in the location where the worker is posted or where the services are to be rendered in Switzerland will process the notification form and are available to answer any questions.

Wie sucht man eine Anstellung in der Schweiz?

Sie können in die Schweiz einreisen und während höchstens sechs Monate eine Anstellung suchen. Für die ersten drei Monate benötigen Sie keine Bewilligung. Anschliessend können Sie eine Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligung EU/EFTA beantragen. Diese gilt für drei Monate pro Jahr; vorausgesetzt ist aber, dass Sie für Ihren Lebensunterhalt aufkommen können.

The Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons (AFMP) between Switzerland and the EU is aimed at liberalising the cross-border provision of services (posted workers or self-employed service providers) for up to 90 effective working days per calendar year. All that is required is prior submission of a notification form. The 90 working days per calendar year rule are calculated both for the company posting workers and for the posted worker.

For services to be rendered beyond this 90-day threshold, a work permit is required. There is no legal entitlement to this permit, however.

Meldefrist von acht Tagen (vor Beginn der Arbeit in der Schweiz)

Die Tätigkeit von entsandten Arbeitnehmenden und selbstständig Erwerbstätigen ist mindestens acht Tage vor dem vorgesehenen Beginn der Arbeiten in der Schweiz zu melden. Nur in klar definierten Notfällen (Reparaturen, Unfällen, Naturkatastrophen oder anderen nicht vorhersehbaren Ereignissen) kann die Arbeit vor der achttägigen Meldefrist aufgenommen werden. Folgende zwei Voraussetzungen müssen jedoch gleichzeitig erfüllt sein:

Der Arbeitseinsatz dient der Behebung eines plötzlich eingetretenen Schadens und hat zum Ziel, weiteren Schaden zu verhindern

Der Arbeitseinsatz erfolgt spätestens drei Tage nach dem Eintritt des Schadens (inkl. Sonn- und Feiertage).
